newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-Hungary sec yields fall, seen flat, lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hungary sec yields fall, seen flat, lower.

text.p: Government securities yields at Hungary's auctions will drop this week, while secondary market yields will be steady to lower after falls following Friday's central bank rate cuts, dealers forecast on Monday.
"The size of the (central bank rate) reductions may provide an opportunity for some further yield falls," said Postabank analyst Attila Torok.
The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) cut on Friday its six-month and 12-month deposit rates by 0.5 percentage point to 20.50 and 20.25 percent respectively.

Dealers said that government securities yields on the secondary market dropped by some 20 basis points after the NBH cuts which had been awaited since a surprise rate hike in March aimed at the protection of savings.
Dealers said one week ago that they expected the deposit rate cuts as Hungary's latest inflation and trade data projected a decline of inflation and interest rates.
On Monday, dealers said that secondary market yields were likely to be flat this week or drop a few basis points after falls following Friday's NBH rate cuts.

"In the past two months the yields hardly moved," said Laszlo Lakatos of Bank Austria Investment. "The yields are substantially lower now...on a market like this a 20 to 30 basis point fall within one day is substantial."

Dealers added that funds placed in one-month reverse repo deals with the NBH may return to the markets following the central bank's 50 basis point repo rate cuts one week ago, and demand created by them may weigh on the yields.
"The question is how much money the repo rate cuts will move," said Lakatos.

Dealers and an analyst added that the markets were expecting a decision for the end of June on a reduction in the monthly forint devaluation rate for the second half of 1997, and this would push yields further down by tens of basis points.
Analysts said earlier this month that a cut of some 0.1 percentage point was likely in the monthly 1.1 percent devaluation rate.

Robert Schutz, Laszlo Lakatos/Bank Austria Investment

NOTE: The Government Debt Management Agency will auction one-month T-bills on Tuesday, three-month T-bills on Wednesday, two-year bonds of the 1999/D series and five-year bonds of the 2001/C series on Thursday.
